utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence wanted to raise a preliminary matter. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. And good morning to everybody in the court. I would like to inform the Trial Chamber that we wanted to have a translation replaced. It is Blagojevic, Mladen's statement, ID922, and the translation which is valid at the moment is 1D180588. This should be replaced by a new translation. The number is 1D191407 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The number is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, just -- could you please check on the transcript whether we have the right number: 1D19407?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat, Your Honours. Mladen Blagojevic's statement is D922. The current translation is 1D180588 [as interpreted]. This should be replaced by the following number: 1D191407 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, which seems to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, can the Prosecution just check it and revert. I'm afraid I'm not in a position to right now, but one of my colleagues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the usual practice is that better translations, if they come from a good source, are admitted and may replace the previous one, and then within 48 hours the other party has an opportunity to revisit that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I state that both numbers are not correctly recorded. The 1D number. They are one digit in addition to the usual numbers. Please repeat, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. [Interpretation] Mladen Blagojevic's statement is D922. The current translation is doc ID 180 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D180588.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The doc ID numbers are always eight digits, same as ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be the correct number. And then it would be replaced by?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D191408 -- 07.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I repeat that last number: 1D191407.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Registrar is instructed to replace the current translation by the newly uploaded one. And the Prosecution has an opportunity to revisit the matter within the next 48 hours. Then, having dealt with that, the witness can be escorted in the courtroom. And, meanwhile, I use the time to briefly address the -- a matter related to Witness Milan Tutoric. On the 3rd of March of this year, the Defence filed a motion to admit the evidence of Witness Milan Tutoric pursuant to Rule 92 ter and Rule 94 bis of the Rules. The Chamber recalls that on the 3rd of December last year, the Prosecution objected to the admission of Milan Tutoric's evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter as requested by the Defence in its 19th November motion on the ground, inter alia, that it contained inadmissible evidence and expert opinion from a witness presented as a witness of fact. On the 18th of December, the Chamber invited the Defence to file an additional submission addressing whether the witness would be more appropriately presented as an expert witness. You can find this at transcript page 30116. The Defence did not file or present any submission at the deadline set by the Chamber. On the 27th of January, 2015, the Chamber denied, without prejudice, the Defence motion to admit the evidence of Milan Tutoric pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this can be found at transcript pages 30674 through 30675. The Chamber is now seized of the 3rd of March motion to admit the evidence of Witness Milan Tutoric. The Chamber understands that the Defence seeks the admission of his evidence pursuant to two rules, two different rules. Unless the Defence wishes to raise further arguments in connection with this matter, the Chamber considers that the Defence is presenting Milan Tutoric as a Rule 94 bis witness and not as a Rule 92 ter witness. Good morning, Mr. Karisik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Our apologies for continuing with an administrative matter when you entered the courtroom. Mr. Karisik, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and I further urge you to focus your answer very much on the questions that are put to you. Ms. Pack will now continue her cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have, please, 65 ter 04050.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay. You can see this on the screen now. It's dated the 12th of July from Dragomir Vasic from the Zvornik CJB. It's to the Bijeljina police forces staff and to the public security department. The public security department, that's you; yes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Read it to yourself, the report, please. You done? Right. So it's about the reporting on the movement of the column of men, isn't it, the first couple of paragraphs, the second and third paragraphs; yes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the dispatch. I know what it is about. In principle, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The last paragraph, please, last sentence, I'll read it out: "We obtained all the above information from the four men we captured in Konjevic Polje an hour ago (at about 1630 hours)." So you knew the MUP were talking to Muslim prisoners from Srebrenica on the 12th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not have any comment on the dispatch, including this part, because this is a report to the Bijeljina sector which does not imply my authority. I was not supposed to react to it. All of these things were happening on the ground and that's where they were dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just pausing there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you again, Witness. The question was whether you had knowledge of this happening, not whether you were in a position where you had to respond or react. That's all not the question. The question is: Did you know that the MUP were talking to Muslim prisoners in -- from Srebrenica on the 12th of July. That's the question. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time I didn't know that. At that time I did not read this dispatch. I was in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You've told us that this report is addressed to you. You're a professional, outstanding professional police ... policeman, and you don't read a report addressed to you from the Zvornik CJB on the 12th July. Is that right? You just didn't read it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time. I had other commitments. I was not duty-bound to read all the dispatches which were not sent to me personally but to the entire department. This is a regular report, and as I can see, it's about people who were taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you didn't read this report because it wasn't addressed to you personally; is that right? Do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd tender this, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7217, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we have, please, P01511.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Right. You can look at the top, see who it is addressed to. And you will be relieved to see that this report from Kijac dated the 13 July 1995 is addressed to you, head, RS MUP Bijeljina, public security department, personally; right? That's you, personally.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to me personally. This is what I read on the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You would have read it because it was addressed to you personally; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I did read it personally. I have to explain why I did not read some of the dispatches, although they -- because they covered some things that I was not involved in. If you will allow me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me just read from the first paragraph of this dispatch. It's addressed to the RS deputy minister of the interior personally. That's Kovac; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: First paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't say Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The RS minister of the interior personally is Kovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you. First paragraph: "During the night of the 12th to the 13th July 1995, members of the VRS and MUP managed to capture a large number of Muslim soldiers (over 300) in ambushes set up in the general Konjevic Polje area." I'm going to go down to about two-thirds of the way down this paragraph and pick it up where it starts: "Earlier" -- it talks about the column and then it goes: "Earlier information regarding their intentions and the axes of movement towards Kladanj and Tuzla (Buljim, Pobudje, Konjevic Polje, Kaldrmica, Cerska, Snagovo, Crni Vrh) has been confirmed many times in interviews with prisoners." So it's not true, is it, Mr. Karisik, what you said yesterday that you didn't know about Muslim prisoners from Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I've said so far is the truth. This is a dispatch sent to the head of department as a regular reporting. In this case, I was not supposed to act upon this dispatch. Some other people were supposed to act upon it. In -- in my case, it was nothing but a regular report on activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I -- no one asked you whether you had to act on it. The question is whether you knew about it. Now, and if you say, I don't have to act upon it, then at least you should know what it is in it in order to know whether you should or should not act on it. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not read a large number of dispatches because I was not at the headquarters. I was in Pale. I told you why I did not read them. I did not read them because there was nothing in them that I should have followed up on. I dealt with entirely different things at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But how would you know that there's nothing in it on which you would have to react if you are not acquainted with the content?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this specific case when it comes to this specific this activity and combat, I did not have any authority or competencies there. I was dedicated to other tasks, and those tasks pertained to the Pale staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not an answer to my question. But I invite Ms. Pack to move on. Please proceed, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Karisik, I'm a little confused because in your statement at paragraph 36 you say -- and I'll read it. You can read it yourself. It's in e-court in the English at page 12. Just if you can look at the hard copy, you say: "I spent most of July 1995 at the RJB headquarters in Bijeljina. I was also a member of the MUP staff in Pale." So is it right, then, that you were in Bijeljina but not in Bijeljina for purposes of picking up written reports about Srebrenica? Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not understand me well. Can I clarify? The seat of the public security sector was in Bijeljina. From the moment the staff was set up in Pale, I spent most of the time first in Pale as a staff member, but occasionally I did go to Bijeljina. On one occasion, I also went to the IKM of the Zvornik Brigade on an order. In other words, I was in Pale, and I was also in Bijeljina. The situation was dramatic, especially in the Sarajevo area. I was both in Pale and in Bijeljina. I can't tell you when I was in any of those places.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me understand another thing. You didn't read this report, this particular report, because you weren't acting on anything concerning Srebrenica. That just wasn't something you were interested in. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I was not interested. I was only interested in the task I was given by the other staff. My role had nothing to do with Srebrenica. These dispatches are nothing but reports on developments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you one thing. You earlier said -- you referred to the moment that the staff was set up in Pale. Could you tell us when exactly that was? What date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After 20 years, I can't give you the exact date when the Pale staff was set up. But I would just like to say that it was sometime in June or the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: That's 1995; right? The year. Just to clarify for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I had no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in 1995, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just reading the ... You said: "From the moment the staff was set up in Pale, I spent most of the time first in Pale as a staff member, but occasionally I did go to Bijeljina." Now your statement reads: "I spent most of July at the RJB headquarters in Bijeljina." And you just told me that that headquarters was in Pale, was set up in June, and that from then on, you spent most of your time in Pale. Now, I've some difficulties in understanding how in July you can spend most of your time in Bijeljina and spent most of your time in Pale. That's slightly unclear to me. Any explanation for what seems to be a contradiction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- I was in Pale in the second half of June. I spent more time in Pale from then on, but during the Sarajevo offensive, I spent more time at the Pale staff in the Sarajevo sector. In the month of July, which is a long month, I spent more time in the Bijeljina sector headquarters, especially in the second half of July. I -- I'm very glad if this is more clear. It says in my statement that I spent more time in the Bijeljina sector in July, yes, because July is a long month. And as for the Pale staff, I was there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, so earlier you -- what apparently you intended to tell us that you spent -- once the Pale headquarters was set up, you spent most of your time in Pale but only in June and not for July. That is then ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the first half of the month of July as well. But it did happen every now and then that I went to the sector for personal and family reasons. Spending time in a different territory was difficult in terms of logistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Right. You didn't read reports about Srebrenica. You didn't act on anything concerning Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's look, please, at 65 ter 32266.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You can see it's to the police forces Command Staff, Pale. So that includes you; right? I'm just asking about the addressee.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just part of the police staff in Pale. One of the members of the staff. Yes. And this is sent to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: 13 July 1995 it's dated. You can see that. And it's from -- and you just need to look at the top for this. It's from the State Security Department, 3rd Administration; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The heading of this document says: RDB, 3rd Administration, Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look, please -- I am not going to read it all out. Let's look at the first paragraph. Now it's not about prisoners, this one. So just take your time and look at that. And you can confirm to me that that's talking about the column of Muslim men. Just the first paragraph. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't manage to read it. I've read half of it. This is a report about the movement of Muslims in that area, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, take your time to read it. And, Ms. Pack, show the patience which, in all fairness, should be given.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Once I've read it, I shall communicate that. It's rather hard for me to read from here. Yes, I've read the first part of the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you. It's about the column of Muslim men; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is about several columns, as far as I could read here. But these are Muslims who are breaking through towards Tuzla, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's look at the last paragraph, please, on that page. And it's page 2 of the English. I'll read it out. Just pay attention: "The latest information obtained from the RDB shows that a Muslim group led by Zulfo Tursunovic this evening arrived in the general sector of Snagovo and established radio communication with members of the so-called Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who are in the sector of Kalesija; hence, it is expected that they engage in joint combat operations ..." And it goes on. And then I'll take it up at the penultimate sentence which is -- we can just go over the page, please, in the B/C/S to page 2. Penultimate sentence of the dispatch, just where it starts: "At the same time the second group of Muslim saboteurs led by Ibrahim Mandzic, aka Mrki, is allegedly in the sector of Gornja Kamenica and moving along the same road along which Tursunovic's group had passed." And it goes on. You received this report, you, Milenko Karisik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Milenko Karisik did not receive that. It was the staff of the police force in Pale that received that but I am part of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: As part of the staff, did you personally receive it, did you read it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I personally did not receive it for sure. It arrives at the duty service there, and if -- if it's something alarming, then the staff should inform the minister who was the only one who has the power to act. Since these forces that were at Srebrenica were under the command of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, you are not invited to expand on who should have received it and should have read it. The simple question was, is whether you received it. Your answer was no, which I take it also means that you haven't read it. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this report, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P7218, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have, please, 65 ter 04086.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, this is a document dated the 13th of July, and it's to Dragomir Vasic. He's the chief of the Zvornik CJB. And it's type-signed from the RJB head, Milenko Karisik; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The name, Milenko Karisik, is typewritten, but my signature is not there, so it is the services of the sector that sent this, but that would be it. It's from the sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, let's just see, shall we, what it says. I'll read the first paragraph: "According to the information available to the RDB, the State Security Department, a Muslim group led by Zulfo Tursunovic, former commander of one of the Muslim brigades from Srebrenica, is currently in the Snagovo sector ..." It goes on. And then just taking the penultimate sentence: "Another group of Muslim extremists led by Ibrahim Mandzic is reportedly in the Gornja Kamenica sector (in the interspace between ..." and it goes on. And it takes up:"... and advancing along the same route previously used by Tursunovic's group." So you see it repeats the content of the previous document that I showed you from the State Security Department about the movement of these two groups in the column of Muslim men from Srebrenica. Can you see that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here -- well, yes I see that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Sir, you've answered my question. Thank you. So you, Milenko Karisik, you, the head of the RJB, received reports about Srebrenica and acted on reports about Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am head of the RJB, and you said that I was head of the RDB, if I heard you correctly. So I am head of the RJB, and from my sector, the dispatch was conveyed to the centre, Vasic, about the information that the RDB had sent to us. So this is a regular thing, and that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this in evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P7219, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we have, please, P2117.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just to clarify, it's a regular thing, is it, that reports go out under your name without you having any knowledge of the contents? Dispatches go out under your name? It's a regular thing, was it, in the RJB?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wanted to say. Only a dispatch that I sign is one that is sent from me personally. Dispatches from the sector, well, are sent further on to those who are proper addressees. In this case, it was the RJB centre, Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It's a teletyped document. They're never signed.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the original document has to bear the signature of the person who is sending it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's look at this document that's up on the screen. It's P2117, dated the 13th July 1995. And it's to the Pale police staff of which you were part; right? Now I would like -- right? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you repeat that question? I didn't understand that you were asking me something.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is to the Pale police staff of which you were part. You were part of the Pale police staff, and this is addressed to the Pale police staff. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the staff in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look, please, at the penultimate paragraph on the page in the B/C/S, and it goes over -- it's over on page 2 in the English translation. It's the second page on page 2 [sic]. You can see this is from Ljubisa Borovcanin; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, down here, it says: Deputy Commander, Ljubisa Borovcanin, yes. Of the special police brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Are you quite sure? Because he hasn't signed it personally. Right? It's on the teleprinter, so it wouldn't be signed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not a big expert for communications, but I cannot confirm what these documents that are before me mean, being that they are not bearing signatures of persons who are sending them. I think that each and every document that is sent has to bear the signature of the person who is sending it. But I accept that this is a document that did exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, in all fairness to the witness, if you ask him, Do you see that Mr. Borovcanin, his name is under it, if the witness then says, Yes, I see that, answering your question, then to say, Are you really sure? Then you're shifting your subject of your questioning. Because you're not asking the witness any further whether he sees that the name of Borovcanin is under it, but you, without clearly announcing that, you're shifting to whether it was sent by Borovcanin, which is a different question. In all fairness to the witness, you shouldn't do that. And a second guidance, if I may give that to you, your questions will not lose strength if you use your voice in such a way that no one could even think of it being used perhaps a bit too strongly, or that it could never come to anyone's mind that the tone of your voice is having some intimidating effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: If you read this paragraph, the second paragraph: "In the night between the 12 and 13 July 1995, this armed Muslim group launched an attack in the direction of Konjevic Polje. In the combat that lasted several hours and which continued throughout today, the enemy sustained a loss of 200 soldiers who were killed, and we captured, or had surrender to us, around 1500 Muslim soldiers. The number increases by the hour." So you knew that the MUP were taking large numbers of prisoners on the 13 July; right.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I read the dispatch for a simple reason: I cannot remember. Because Ljubisa Borovcanin is directly under the minister of the interior, not the sector. The special brigade is directly under the authority of the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So just to fully understand your evidence: Borovcanin knew about the Muslim prisoners; Vasic knew about the Muslim prisoners; Kovac knew about the Muslim prisoners; Dragan Kijac knew about the Muslim prisoners; but you, you didn't know anything. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't know. Because I do not have the authority to act because I was dealing with my own assignments, things that I had been ordered to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you've told us that several times. It's sufficient you say you didn't know, and why you didn't know is sometimes relevant; but here, most important, is that you say you didn't know. And that dispatches sent under your name, you had no knowledge of their content. Is that -- at least for the one that we saw, that's true, isn't it? Yes, you had no knowledge of what was sent and what we saw was sent under your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember exactly what I personally saw because it's been over 20 years. But for some reasons that you did not exactly allow me to speak about, I did not follow this because it's outside my line of work, and I had a specific task as head of the sector to do some other work in the staff in Pale, not to deal with Srebrenica. And I also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you've told us that now five times. So to say that we didn't allow you to explain that, we allowed you to briefly explain. You did so. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Mr. Karisik, the evidence in this case is that the public security policemen were involved in escorting the convoy of thousands of Muslim men - prisoners - from Bratunac to Zvornik on the 14th of July. Is that something else that you didn't know about at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't know that because I did not have authority to act. The unit is resubordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska in combat action, and they receive tasks on the spot there, and then they're outside the command structure of the Ministry of Interior, and they also are not under my authority then.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Did it surprise you on the 16th of July, since you weren't interested or doing anything related to Srebrenica, when Kovac ordered you to go to Zvornik to meet with Pandurevic? That come as a surprise?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not surprised by any order received from the minister. It is my obligation to carry out orders received from the minister. He is my superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Meet Dragomir Vasic at the Zvornik CJB. He briefed you about the situation and problems concerning Zvornik. That's in your statement. Is that right? Your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: He sent written reports on the 12th and 13th July, and he's met with -- he was at meeting on 13th of July in Bratunac with Beara and Deronjic, and they talked about the plan to murder Muslim men. That's the evidence in this case. You didn't talk about that, the planned execution of Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And at the Zvornik Brigade forward command post you met Vinko Pandurevic and you spent several hours with him. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we have a reference for "that it is evidence in this case" of the discussions between Colonel Beara and Vasic. Because, in talking with my colleague, I do not recall the same having been led in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, I'll give the reference. It's M. Nikolic, T11952 to 11953. And I said he was present at a meeting at the SDS office in Bratunac on the 13 July when Beara and Deronjic talked about the plan to murder the Muslim men. That's for transcript references. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: We'll just go to Vinko Pandurevic, please. So just to pick up the question that you didn't have the chance to answer. It was that you met Vinko Pandurevic at the Zvornik Brigade forward command post and sent several hours with him there, is that right, on the 16th July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. I'm a direct participant there and it is easier for me to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, you gave a reference, the page reference, with respect to Momir Nikolic. Could you repeat that. It was not recorded. And for the sake of Mr. Ivetic, this would be helpful to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It was transcript reference T11952 to 11953.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Pandurevic also briefed you about the situation and problems in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, not particularly, except for this enormous column of Muslim soldiers that is moving. Nothing, in particular.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So he talked about the situation related to the column. That's what you say?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm saying that he told me that this large column had taken a policeman prisoner. And that is the reason why I came on orders from the minister to Pandurevic to his forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we look, please, quickly at P01497.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It's in manuscript and I hope can you read it. We see it's dated 15th of July, 1995 and it's an interim combat report to the Drina Corps Command. And over the page, you'll see -- if we can just quickly look over the page, you'll see it's from Vinko Pandurevic, the commander. We can just look briefly at pages 2 in both the English translation and the B/C/S before reverting back. It's from, you can see written there, Vinko Pandurevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it is in handwriting, and it says: Commander, Vinko Pandurevic. That's the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And we'll stay on page 2 in the B/C/S and go back to page 1 in the English. I want to look at the fourth paragraph in the English. And in the B/C/S, it's the second and third paragraphs on that page 2. English, it's fourth and fifth. I'll read them. It says: "An additional burden for us is the large number of prisoners distributed throughout schools in the brigade area, as well as obligations of security and restoration of the terrain? "This command cannot take care of these problems any longer, as it has neither the material nor other resources. If no one takes on this responsibility, I will be forced to let them go." So that's the report that Pandurevic sends the day before he meets with you, spends several hours with you in Zvornik. My question: When he talked to you that day, on the 16th July, did he not say, One of the problems in Zvornik, in addition to the column, fighting the column, is the fact that the VRS are busy executing and burying prisoners, and they've been doing this for three days. It has been a burden for us. Did he not say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object. That does not arise from the document and the section that the counsel has cited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there a suggestion that this is from the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I didn't say this was from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It says: So that's that report Pandurevic sends, and then she asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. "And then my question: When he talked to you on that day." That is, there is a relation between the document and the question, but there's no suggestion in the question itself that that is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then it's a compound question and it's confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I fully agree with that. Could you please split it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: When you met Pandurevic and you spent several hours with him on the 16th July, did he mention that the VRS had been executing and burying prisoners for three days?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't discuss that, and I never reported on that either.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is time for a break. We'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back, Mr. Karisik, after the break. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you on schedule, as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I think it's about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then you even stay within your time estimates. We take a break, and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to say I didn't realise that I had -- apologies for interrupting. Just to say I didn't realise that I had 45 minutes of my allotted time before we broke, and I'm not going to take all of that, but I will be more than 15 minutes, I hope less than half an hour, but I didn't realise I had so much time when you asked the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not so much time, therefore, I'll use part of most of it, but what do I really need to put the questions that are relevant for us and then to see whether that can be done in as little time as possible. That's the two different approaches.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the second one is the one the Chamber prefers. But please move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I will be as quick as I can and that is my intention, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not too quick. Not too quick, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Karisik, can we look, please, at 65 ter 19565. Now, just as we're looking at this, can you confirm, on the face of it, that this is a document dated the 16th of July from a member of the police forces Command Staff in Pale?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And if we look at the substance, the first paragraph says, I'll read it out: "Please be informed that today at around 1500 hours we were informed by Assistant Karisik about negotiations between the command of the VRS and enemy forces from Srebrenica and the 2nd Turkish Corps from Tuzla on the passage of the Turkish troops through a part of the territory of Zvornik municipality in the direction of Kalesija. The command of the VRS is represented in the negotiations by Colonel Vinko Pandurevic ..." And it goes on. Now, Assistant Karisik, that's you; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You informed the police forces Command Staff by 1500 hours about Pandurevic's negotiations with the ABiH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure that after the end of my mission with Pandurevic, I had an obligation to report to the staff, and the dispatch actually confirms that I complied with that obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7220 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, in your statement at paragraph 62 - you have it in front of you - in the English, in e-court, it's page 18. You've talked about it. You say you were aware that Pandurevic opened the corridor on 16th July but you don't recall if you had direct contact with the president - that's Karadzic - about this. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't have any contacts with President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, you've been asked about this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And could we please have up 65 ter 32252. And we want, please, page 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And I'm asking to have shown here the transcript of your testimony in the Karadzic case. And it's in English, so I'll read it to you slowly. From line 14. "Q. ... in your statement at paragraph 62, you say you don't remember if you had direct contact with Mr. Karadzic that day. Mr. Karadzic in this trial stated at 26265, lines 1 to 4: "'Thank you. Did you perhaps find out that Mr. Karisik phoned me to inform me of this move of Pandurevic's?' "Does that help you remember that you called and spoke with Mr. Karadzic directly? "A. This, unfortunately not. My technical capacities were very poor. I was in a mountainous area and I wasn't really able to sit down and have a conversation with Mr. Karadzic, truly." Now, is that your truthful testimony, because you've told us you contacted the Pale police forces Command Staff that day before 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object now that's she doing a compound question. If she's going to present a part of the transcript and ask if that is truthful, that's one question. Everything else that comes later is confusing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Is that your truthful testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to reporting to Mr. Karadzic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: But it's right --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is truthful.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It is right, isn't it, that you were able to - and did - report to the Pale police forces staff before 1500 hours on 16th July, like we just saw?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember the time. I believe it was after 1500 hours. They also say "around 1500 hours." It was not before that. I first needed to report to the minister through the staff about my mission, what's -- what its nature was, and that it wasn't completed successfully. This is not contained in the dispatch. I didn't contact the staff from the forward command post. I only did it when I was able to do it, when I got hold of some communications means. This is the whole truth. I could not report to President Karadzic from the forward command post, neither do I remember that I ever did that. There was no need or obligation for me to report to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: That wasn't the question where you reported from. The question was whether you reported.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Reported to whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Karadzic. This is what you were asked in the Karadzic case. You said you had no direct contact with Karadzic that day. That's the question. Not where you contacted Karadzic from but whether you contacted Karadzic. You understand? Right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand your question. My answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please have P01338. Actually, this is being -- is under seal so if it could not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, you've been shown this before. It's dated the 16th of July, 1995. And it's an intercept of a conversation between the Main Staff duty officer and General Mladic which takes place at 1615 hours. And I'll read it. Starts: "Good day, General, sir. "Well, it's like this."

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: "Good day, General, sir." Continues: "Well, it's like this. I've just sent a telegram to Toso. Well, the president called a short while ago and said that he had been informed by Karisik that Pandurevic has arranged passage for the Muslims over to that territory. Since I have no communication with him, I asked the duty officer to urgently connect me with him; to have him send me a telegram with that information and not to do anything without authorisation until he receives our answer. Now I'm waiting for them to call me because Pandurevic hasn't called for the last four ..." And it continues: "Yes, of course. But, but there are both fighters and civilians. And then it goes on: "Nobody is playing around, that's just the information we got." And then it goes on. Karisik, that's you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Does this refresh your memory? You were in Zvornik to inform the president what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. It is correct that I was in Zvornik but it is not correct that I reported to President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about one more document; it's P01586. This is another document you've seen before. It's dated the 16th of January, 1996. It's addressed to the RJB public security department head. That's you, isn't it still, in January 1996?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And also, as we can see, to the Main Staff of the VRS sector for intelligence and security, intelligence administration (for information). You can see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not very legible, but still I can read it. There's some yellow stains all over the document. At least in my case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, I'll read it out to make it easier. First paragraph: "Please find enclosed the full text of a dispatch from the Main Staff VRS Main Staff sector for intelligence and security, intelligence administration ..." And if goes on: "To the Ministry of Interior, the minister personally." Goes on: "Considering that we have a group of members in the 10th Sabotage Detachment who are foreign citizens or are on a list of individuals who have been indicted by The Hague Tribunal, we ask that you order the Bijeljina MUP to issue personal IDs with Serbian first and last names to these individuals, or with different first and last names for Serbian nationals, there are 8 ... such individuals." We go over the page in the English, we see that quoted dispatch is from Chief Colonel Petar Salapura. You are remembered -- and this is addressed to you, of course, to act on the request by the VRS Main Staff signed the minister, Dragan Kijac. Just a question about Kijac. Kijac, who had been your counterpart, head of the DB in July 1995, was by then minister; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So the minister orders you to issue fake IDs?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minister sends to the sector an order to issue documents for the intelligence service of the VRS. This is part of co-operation between two organs or two institutions in Republika Srpska. My role was to forward this to the competent administration so that the obligation could be complied with.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And, indeed, the obligation was complied with; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm as I sit here what the ultimate outcome was. I did not get any feedback as how much was accomplished. But as head of the -- of that department, I obviously issued an order for the minister's request to be followed through. That was my obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You know that members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment executed Muslim men at Branjevo farm in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know who members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment were or what they did. I didn't have that information. That was not the nature of my knowledge at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The evidence in this case from one member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment who admitted taking part in mass executions is that he was indeed issued a fake ID. You, head of the public security department of The MUP of Republika Srpska, were protecting these men from The Hague Tribunal; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is no. I just carried out a procedure that is based on the law, that is lawful, from the minister of the interior who had received a request. What that is customary co-operation between services that a certain number of IDs, I mean, we didn't really take into account who they were, what they were. We weren't interested in that. I don't know that now either what it was that they did or individual, et cetera. My professional duty was to forward the request and to have this co-operation between the two organs, the two institutions carried out. Of course, there were records kept and in that administration there is a certain procedure as to how this is supposed to be done. So it is possible to check what was carried out and to what extent and whether all of it had been carried out at all. Afterward, I did not deal with the question of implementation. For me it was a routine thing to carry out an order from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pack. I have one question in relation to the last matter that was addressed by Ms. Pack. You're emphasizing your obligations. Do you feel you have any obligation not to obstruct justice to be rendered by a court which was founded by the Security Council?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time I was not thinking about this, what you are referring to now. I didn't know about that either. I wasn't interested in the names or who they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it was clear from this document, I think - but tell me if you understand that otherwise - that it was to shield them from prosecutions in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't want to comment on Salapura's dispatch and the intelligence service of the military security. We probably as a different organ of the Ministry of Interior acted and that is customary co-operation. That's what matters to me. Now as for the rest, I really cannot say anything about that, and I didn't think about that. I'm a professional. That is what my powers were and I did that. Of course, in that administration, there is a special procedure, so if there is a problem, then the true identity can be established and so on, but that is a question for a different witness. As head of the sector, I carried out the minister's order and that is that, and I cannot give any further comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're moving away from my question. My question is whether your obligations not to obstruct justice, which was established by the Security Council, would not prevail over your duty to obey orders from your minister, especially if those orders clearly seem to allude to the action required by you -- required to be taken by you would be instrumental to such obstruction of justice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is that I am carrying out the procedure of the Ministry of Interior and enforcing the law. That is my obligation on the basis of the law. I did not think about any further implications, and there was no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I understand you well, you say, I thought about the law, which you followed, and you didn't think about the law which may have imposed obligations upon you as well, but you just did not think about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the term that you used "promislijo"; "thought." I said that I carried out the orders issued to me by the minister and that is in accordance with the law and the rules in my ministry, and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of possibly obligations that are imposed under international law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, at that point in time, no. Obviously. But as head of the public security sector, I'm duty-bound to carry out the procedures of work of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you've told us that now three times. Last question: Were you aware of the existence of this Tribunal in early 1996, January 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that I was aware of that. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This -- this last answer takes me back to questions that were put to you in relation to paragraph 62 of your statement. Today, I think you clearly testified that you had not directly contacted President Karadzic about the corridor, the column of Muslims moving out. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, you do not say you had no contact. In your statement, you say: "I do not recall if I had direct contact." What made you change your mind in relation to what is found in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand in what way I changed my mind? What do you mean changed my mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll explain to you. If I say, I don't recall whether I was at location A yesterday, that means it could be yes; it could be no. If I say, I was not at location A yesterday, that's only one possibility. That is, I wasn't there. Now, in your statement, you leave it open whether you had or whether you had not direct contact with President Karadzic about the corridor because you say, I don't recall if I had. Today you say, I had not, which is not the same. Do you have any explanation for this change as I just explained it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my paragraph 62, I said that I do not remember having contacted President Karadzic. That is what I confirm today as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Let me show you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not contact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not the same. If you don't understand that, then there are other instances where you also said, I don't remember, and then later say it didn't happen, which is not the same. I had hoped you would understand it. If you do not, then that -- we'll have to consider that when evaluating your evidence. If you have no further explanation and if you say it's just the same, then we'll move on and I'll give an opportunity to Mr. Ivetic to put further questions to you. Oh, but perhaps first Judge Moloto may have one or more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to follow up on some of the issues that Judge Orie raised on the question of this order from the minister. Within your duties in the department where you were working, was it also so that you were obliged to carry out orders which were unlawful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And -- you have answered me. Thank you so much. You do not see this order as unlawful? To order somebody to make fake IDs to people? Isn't that unlawful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the request of one security service, one organ, that is, to another, is legal legitimate and lawful, and we are duty-bound to respond to that request for co-operation that is based on the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What I'm asking you is the content of the order that you're co-operating on. You say it's unlawful, is it not? Is it not unlawful to ask that fake IDs be issued to people? I'm not asking about co-operation with other departments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not unlawful if the Ministry of the Interior is responding to requests for co-operation from the intelligence service of the Army of Republika Srpska. These are not unlawful doings. This is something that exists anywhere in the world, that kind of co-operation. The issuing of such documents is not unlawful. On our side, we do not go into who they are, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I stop you there. You say it's not unlawful to respond. I'm not asking you to respond. I'm saying is it not unlawful to order that fake IDs be issued? That's the question. I'm not talking about your co-operation. I'm talking about the order. To order fake IDs to be issued: Is that lawful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is our obligation to do that for a different organ, that a certain number of IDs and number of documents should be done. I don't think that is unlawful. I think that all security services in the world do that for individuals for whom it is necessary to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... stop you. You either want to answer my question or you don't want to answer it. My question has nothing to do with what co-operation you're obliged to give. I'm asking you is an order by a superior that is -- says issue fake IDs is that a lawful order in your understanding of the law? If you -- it's either yes or no, and I realise that you are not answering my question, and I stop at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would direct you to page 37, line 2 where the witness answered your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 37 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 37, line 2: I don't think that it is unlawful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's talking about something different, Mr. Ivetic, with all due respect. He starts by saying: "It is our obligation to do that for a different organ that a certain number of IDs and a number of documents should be done. I don't think it's unlawful." I'm not asking him about whether he should do something. I'm asking him about whether the order he received is lawful.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in my position, Your Honours, he has answered that by saying, I don't think that is unlawful, I think that all [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm telling you he hasn't answered me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's some ambiguity there in what the witness says is unlawful. Do I understand your answer to be that not under all circumstances ordering to issue a fake ID is considered to be unlawful? Did you hear my question or did you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Translation is still going, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is that the order of the minister is not unlawful. That is my only comment. I have no other comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- that's an answer to the question. Mr. Ivetic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can stay with this document and this topic for the time being, let's take a step backwards in time to the time-period before the war when the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had jurisdiction over the entirety of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In your opinion with such an order to have fake IDs issued to intelligence personnel, would that have been a type of order that the SFRY -- SFR Bosnia-Herzegovina would have undertake prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's a very leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. Would you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could have assistance I don't see where it is leading when taking back to a time-period prior to the war. Such questions to establish a time-period are permitted in direct examination according to my understanding of trial procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I didn't understand it to be a question about time, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I won't respond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clearly hinting at what you expect to be the answer. In that respect, it is leading. Please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if such fake IDs would have been issued in due course by the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina prior to the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer and my opinion is yes. Because this is customary co-operation in all countries of the world regarding changes of IDs with different names and surnames, and that is done by all police forces in the world. In the war, before the war, after the war, to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now this order, if we can go back to the first page in English, and if we could scroll up to the top in the B/C/S, this is dated in the year 1996. Sir, do you know when the Law on Co-operation with the ICTY Tribunal was enacted on either -- on the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but I think it is after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the parties certainly are in a position to agree on whether a certain law was enacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would offer a stipulation for the Prosecution to concur that it was enacted in 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that we don't have do deal with that court at this moment. I cannot imagine the parties cannot agree when a certain act was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But Your Honours' questions to the witness talks about unlawfulness of an order talks about co-operation with the ICTY; therefore, it is germane to this testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, there is more than domestic laws having been adopted. If it was as simple as that, then we might perhaps have an easier job. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can move to another topic, you were asked about a number of dispatches -- or about dispatches that were sent to your office. One of which was P7217. And I want to ask you, sir, based upon your position within the public security sector in 1995, do you have an estimate of the number of documents, dispatches, or other reports that would be addressed to your position as one of the recipients, among others in the MUP, from across the country in the normal course of business in a day, a week, or any time-period that you can assist us with?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you're saying. The RJB is the largest structure, the most numerous one, with the largest subject matter dealt with within the Ministry of Interior. When the police is used in combat operations, there was an enormous number of dispatches arriving every day and the administrations reacted in accordance with their authority and carried out work in the domain of publish law and order, the crime-prevention police, checking border crossings, traffic, protecting people and their property is our constitutional duty otherwise as well and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir you were asked for a number, an estimate of the number, not describing the whole structure. How many per day or per week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say exactly what that number is. Maybe the analytics department could say about that period, but the security subject matter dealt with by the ministry involved great -- a great many dispatches from Trebinje to Banja Luka. So the chief of communications would have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I proceed, Your Honour, or do you have anything? If we can now look at P3009.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This was shown to you during cross-examination. This document from Momcilo Mandic is dated the 31st of March, 1992. Was the special police unit divided and split already by this date, the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The date of the 27th of March, 1992 is being referred to here. The unit disbanded in the evening on the 4th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did this dispatch have immediate effect upon the special police unit, or were any additional steps required to be received by the special police unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that level then in this joint unit, I did not receive this dispatch personally. Perhaps it was sent to the commander of the unit, but he didn't show it to me. And this dispatch -- well, quite a bit of time went by. I've already referred to the dates. And we stayed in this joint formation and obviously this was not addressed to us on the basis of the date when this was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at transcript pages 33161 and 33163, you were directed to your statement talking about the agreement on the splitting of the MUP and how it was in keeping with the Lisbon-Cutileiro Plan. Let's first talk in terms of the Cutileiro Plan. What was your understanding of how the Cutileiro Plan applied to what was going on in the MUP at that time, the Republic of Bosnia MUP at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Cutileiro Plan is a plan that envisaged a new internal set-up within Bosnia-Herzegovina. As far as I know, in this plan, in its chapters, there was this important thing that had to do with the Ministry of Interior or, rather, the police. And all three communities, all three ethnic communities, all three peoples, on the basis of that plan, could set up their own police force in the area where they were a majority. This plan was signed by the highest representatives of the Muslim, Croat and Serb peoples. Unfortunately, Serbs carried out that plan; but, unfortunately, as far as I know, the Muslim representative on the plane backtracked and withdrew his approval, whichever way you want to put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can call up D935. That should be your statement, which I think I still have in front of you. And if we could turn to page 7 in the Serbian, page 6 in the English, and I'd like to focus on paragraph 19 of the same. And, sir, focussing on the Serbian original which you signed, in the English translation, it says: "In keeping with the Treaty of Lisbon/Cutileiro Plan," were you talking about a treaty in the Serbian original or a -- what -- could you read for us what it says in the Serbian original as to that passage where the Cutileiro Plan is identified.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the agreement reached at the top echelons of the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Serbian special police was given the base in Vrace in the school of the Ministry of Interior. Whereas, the Muslim and Croatian part of the special police remained in Krtelje. That was about the decision which was passed at Minister Delimustafic's level and co-ordinated with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We seem to have missed the part that I was focussing on. Could you read for us what appears in the Serbian, what words appear in the Serbian just before Cutileiro Plan, the other part of how the -- the two word that appear before Cutileiro Plan?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What appears is the wording in keeping with the Lisbon Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand the -- the portion properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is what I was referring to as in the English, it says the Lisbon Treaty. Now I'd like to look at P3106 in e-court. In e-court, this Prosecution document has been identified as: "Statement of principles for new constitutional arrangements of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Lisbon Agreement." And if we can go to page 3 in both versions, this is dated 18 March 1992 and is -- says at the bottom: "As agreed by the leaders of SDA, SDS, and HDZ parties in the fifth round of the talks on future constitutional arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina under the auspices of the EC Peace Conference." Is this the Cutileiro Plan/Lisbon Agreement that you are referencing in this paragraph of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My opinion is that this is a part of the Lisbon Treaty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 4, the very next page, there is a map here that gives designations for Muslim, Serb and Croat. Are you familiar with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could I just interrupt you. I understood the issue raised in cross-examination was whether or not there was a -- a final agreement which could be applied, rather than there was any discussion about what the Cutileiro Plan, applicable or not, would encompass and including, maps, et cetera, I'm not aware of any map issue being raised. So, therefore, I'm wondering whether I misunderstood the cross-examination or what makes you think that this issue is triggered by the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understood they were requesting the existence of the citation in the statement primarily saying that there was no treaty which we've now seen as a result of imprecise translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: As I remember I'm just trying to finds the reference, but I think I actually referred to the statement of principles in terms. And then didn't ask questions about the detail because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was about whether it had become final, whether it was binding upon the parties and that's -- and therefore whether you could talk about a treaty, whether it was concluded yes or no, not about the content of what was drafted and this one would have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes. And the follow-up was whether it was agreed the MUP was divided [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that's another matter whether that there was agreement among the parties. So, therefore, I think, Mr. Ivetic, the maps, et cetera, is not a matter which is in dispute at this moment in this context. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. I just stress that the Prosecution's own exhibit calls it the Lisbon Agreement; just so we're clear on that. If we can turn to -- well, actually, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's quite a number of questions in cross-examination about whether the splitting of the special police unit and the sending of the Serb part to Vrace was known or agreed to by the collegium of the MUP. I would again ask for 1D5309 to be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I wasn't talking about the special unit in cross-examination. There were four question about the division of the MUP and it was just these two documents, so I think to then go back and talk again about the special unit would not really be re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not doing any questions; I'm just making a submission again as to the associated exhibit. Your Honours, if it assists I can shorten the 16 pages of that document by saying pages 5 through 8 -- actually 5 through 11, 5 through 11 encompass the entire process of that and I would revise our request for that associated exhibits to be admitted limiting it to those pages, 5 and through exclusive 11. And I think it's now appropriate to have that tendered and admitted based upon the cross-examination of the Prosecution on this very same area, relying upon a 1992 dispatch of Mr. Alija Delimustafic who is the person giving the testimony in 1D5309.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, any objection against ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I maintain the position, the Prosecution maintains the position that this extract of testimony from apparently from Delimustafic in the State Court is neither relevant nor probative to the extent -- or, indeed, an inseparable and indispensable part of the testimony. I don't see how it assists. But perhaps I need to read the paragraphs that my friend is now relying on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the pages were given yesterday so, therefore, you had an opportunity already. I do understand that the Defence wants to establish that Mr. Delimustafic -- but not only him. There is more than just the statement of Mr. Delimustafic, Mr. Ivetic, but at least in one point in time he describes the process as he did in that courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the Chamber was just wondering whether on what basis it will now be admitted. You said it is a document which sheds additional light on -- on -- well, perhaps you explain exactly what the procedural position of the Defence is in this respect and also in relation to whether any questions were put to the witness about what now appears to be the content of the document you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And please repeat the correct number. It was not recorded properly. I think it is 1D05309; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct. So 1D05309 is an associated document, associated with paragraph 19 of the witness' statement, which we originally tendered as an associated exhibit. After questions were asked of the witness of his knowledge of Mr. Delimustafic's comments, Your Honours suggested that now the testimony of the witness could stand in place of the document. And I agreed with you. Then the Prosecution cross-examined the witness presenting documents that pre-date the 2001 testimony of Delimustafic, implying that was no agreement at the collegium level and that there -- and that Delimustafic was -- was ordering that the units that the MUP not be split. And so for purposes of understanding the witness's testimony in 19 and assessing the credibility of the witness's testimony in relation to 19 and in relation to the answers to the questions in cross-examination I'm now re-raising 1D05309, the page selection that I identified, as it is directly relevant and directly tied to the questions that were posed to him in cross-examination and helps the Chamber to assess the testimony of the witness given during that cross-examination. And it's for that limited purpose, not for the truth of the matter asserted in the document 1D5309.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I still don't understand why it is being admitted -- sought to be admitted not for the truth, but I understand it's being sought to be admitted to corroborate what the witness is saying about a few incidents not -- so -- I am -- I think it is being sought to be admitted for its truth. I mean, that's the point is that it's a transcript of what this individual says, which as I understand it the Defence says corroborates the witness. Now the point really is just a point of principle, is whether it's really and truly is indispensable and inseparable to this witness's testimony to put in somebody else's testimony in another case that apparently - so the Defence says - supports what he is saying.
